summary.headline: Krsnaa Diagnostics Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR271 crore, but PAT grew only 3% to INR25 crore as margins eased.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR271 crore, up 32% YoY and the company's highest quarterly revenue, with H1 revenue at INR507 crore (up 27%). EBITDA before CSR and ESOP rose about 20% to INR72 crore, but margin fell to 27% from 29% as upfront costs for new projects (mainly Rajasthan) and higher depreciation and finance costs weighed. Receivables rose to about INR470 crore at September 30, and management cited visibility of about INR200 crore of collections in Q3. Management is pushing cash-based PPP and retail to lift the revenue mix and cash generation.

segments.name: PPP and institutional business
segments.commentary: Network of 259 pathology labs and 196 CT/MRI centers across 19 states and UTs, covering 334+ districts with about 75% of centers in rural areas. Rajasthan implementation is about 75-80% complete by labs; test volumes nearly doubled sequentially but revenue per test fell more than 30% QoQ on Rajasthan and radiology ramp-up.

segments.name: Retail (RPL)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue about INR23.5 crore, up about 35% YoY; patient volume up 45%, test volume up 48%. Retail is about 9% of group revenue and is operationally breakeven as of September; management targets absolute EBITDA breakeven by Q3-early Q4 and positive retail EBITDA exiting FY27.

guidance_outlook: Expects cash-based revenues to reach about 40-45% of revenue mix by FY27 end, roughly INR400 crore for the year; current share about 35-38%.
Targets retail at double-digit share of revenue by FY27 end, then about 20%-plus in two to three years.

Rajasthan can deliver about INR250 crore annualised; most of that expected in FY28, with partial progress in FY27. Management expects EBITDA margin uptick as revenue ramps and costs do not scale proportionately.
Targets working capital days back to historical 90-100 days through collections and cash PPP mix.

Aspires to ROCE in the high teens, using sale-leaseback, cash businesses and cost optimisation; new growth levers include PET-CT Punjab PPP, 34 CT scans in Himachal Pradesh (15+ year tenders) and the Apulki hospital tie-up (about 2,000 beds).
capex_capacity: Rajasthan lab and collection-centre deployment about 75-80% complete; additional labs requested by government are being implemented.
Entered specialised PET/CT through PPP route; PET-CT project in Punjab is cash-based.
Won tender for 34 CT machines in Himachal Pradesh, cash-based; part of planned pipeline.
Apulki Healthcare hospital in Pune has commenced operations; further hospital PPPs in Borivali, PCMC, KDMC and Chembur-Govandi.
Some sites still pending lab deployment and collection centres, adding depreciation ahead of revenue.
demand_pricing: Test volumes grew strongly YoY and nearly doubled sequentially, driven by Rajasthan PPP ramp-up, radiology projects in Maharashtra and retail activations.
Blended revenue per test fell more than 30% QoQ; management attributes this to lower-priced Rajasthan PPP volumes and expects it to recover as projects mature.
Fees to hospitals and channel partners are rising, linked to Rajasthan revenues, while consumables, reagents and employee costs were cut.

Cash-based PPP share is partly selective and partly driven by states preferring cash when budget allocations are short; margins are similar at project level, but better at company level due to lower financing cost.
Payables rose from INR63 crore to INR230 crore, comprising trade creditors and capex-related creditors.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rajasthan cost base fully in P&L, and can it reach about INR250 crore annualised run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most cost has already hit P&L with only incremental manpower and consumables to come, and most depreciation is booked. Annualised Rajasthan potential is about INR250 crore, with most of it expected in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the confidence in collecting about INR200 crore of receivables in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the delays are concentrated in a few states (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Himachal Pradesh) while Assam and Odisha pay on time. Confirmations from government sources support collection in Q3, though management admitted Q3 collections have historically been on the higher side.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue per test falling while volumes surge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to lower-priced Rajasthan PPP volumes and radiology ramp-up, and said revenue per test will rise as these mature. Test volume split and centre count were deferred to offline follow-up.

qa_highlights.question: Current cash-based share and 3-year target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current cash-based share is about 35-38%, with a 40-45% target by year-end. Management is working toward more than 50%, with further cash PPP tender announcements expected soon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to double-digit ROCE in the high teens, citing sale-leaseback, cash businesses and cost optimisation as levers. No specific two-year figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Retail EBITDA breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail was operationally breakeven around September. Absolute breakeven including marketing is targeted for Q3-early Q4, with positive retail EBITDA exiting FY27.

risks_watch: Receivables of about INR470 crore and whether the INR200 crore Q3 collection visibility materialises, especially from Maharashtra, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh.
Margin trajectory: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 27% and PAT rose only 3%; watch for operating leverage as Rajasthan matures.
Blended revenue per test declining as lower-priced PPP volumes grow.
Rising payables (INR230 crore) and working capital days, which management aims to return to 90-100 days.
Retail breakeven timing and the 40-45% cash-revenue target by FY27 end.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, pipeline and long-term conviction, but cautious and at times evasive on receivables timing, margins and detailed splits (volume mix, centre count, Rajasthan revenue), which were deferred offline.
key_quotes: For the first time, Krsnaa Diagnostics has crossed INR500 crores in revenue in the last 6 months, achieving INR507 crores in H1 FY '27.
We see this money to be collected in the Q3 with a very strong conviction and confidence based on certain confirmations and assurances that we've received from various authorities.
By the end of FY '27, we expect our cash-based revenues to contribute almost 40% to 45% of the overall revenue mix, aggregating to approximately INR400 crores for the year.
And we are exiting FY '27 with the sheer positive EBITDA numbers for the retail front.

growth.why: Management guides cash-based revenue to ~INR400 cr (40-45% mix) in FY27 and Rajasthan to ~INR250 cr annualised mostly in FY28, backed by Rajasthan deployment 75-80% complete, a won 34-CT Himachal tender and ~INR200 cr Q3 collections visibility, but no revenue growth percentage was guided and revenue per test fell >30% QoQ.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects EBITDA margin uptick as Rajasthan revenue ramps and costs don't scale; Q2 margin was 27% vs 29% YoY, with most Rajasthan cost and depreciation already in P&L.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Rajasthan lab and collection-centre deployment is 75-80% complete, with additional government-requested labs being implemented, and Apulki hospital (Pune) has commenced operations; some sites still pending lab deployment.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Test volumes nearly doubled QoQ and grew strongly YoY, with retail patient volume up 45% and test volume up 48%; Rajasthan PPP ramp-up and Maharashtra radiology projects drive further growth, though no revenue growth % was guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No formal new capex guided; cash-based PPP tenders (34 CT in Himachal Pradesh, PET-CT in Punjab, further hospital PPPs in Borivali, PCMC, KDMC, Chembur-Govandi) are new growth levers and management expects more cash PPP tender announcements soon, but utilisation was not quantified.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance raise discussed; the company gave cash-mix (40-45%, ~INR400 cr) and retail targets but flagged receivables of ~INR470 cr and Q3 collection visibility of only ~INR200 cr as the key uncertainty.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables rose to ~INR470 cr with delays in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh, Q3 collection of ~INR200 cr is unconfirmed, and revenue per test fell >30% QoQ; PAT grew only 3% YoY to INR25 cr.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PET-CT Punjab PPP (cash-based) and 34 CT scans in Himachal Pradesh are approved and expected to come online, with retail targeting absolute EBITDA breakeven by Q3-early Q4 FY27 — these are new service lines rather than launches with dates.

rows.label: Working capital days back to 90-100
rows.why: Receivables rose to ~INR470 cr and payables jumped from INR63 cr to INR230 cr; management targets 90-100 days via collections and cash PPP mix, but Q3 collections of ~INR200 cr are only visibility, not confirmed.

rows.label: Cash-based revenue mix to 40-45%
rows.why: Cash-based share is ~35-38% today and management targets 40-45% (~INR400 cr) by FY27 end, with working toward more than 50% and further cash PPP tenders expected soon.

rows.label: Retail absolute EBITDA breakeven
rows.why: Retail (~9% of revenue, Q2 revenue ~INR23.5 cr, up ~35% YoY) is operationally breakeven as of September, with absolute breakeven targeted in Q3-early Q4 and positive retail EBITDA exiting FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the cash-PPP pipeline and Rajasthan ramp-up, but cautious and at times evasive on receivables timing, margins and detailed volume/centre splits, which were deferred offline; analysts pressed on Q3 collections and why revenue per test is falling.
